name: LBNL 2014 US PUE by space type - closet: 2.0 (component sum: 1 | 0.05 | - | 0.93 | 0.02 -> IT 1, no transformer, UPS 0.93, cooling 0.02, lighting 0.02)
unit: PUE ratio (total facility energy / IT equipment energy), 2014 baseline
methodology: MODELED BASELINE, TABLE 4 ('2014 PUE by Space Type') of the DOE/BL United States Data Center Energy Usage Report. The row decomposes total PUE into IT (=1 by definition), transformer, UPS, cooling and lighting contributions, and the components sum to the stated total - which is how the table was verified here rather than trusted. Space types are IDC-defined and span both internal enterprise spaces and service-provider spaces; the report states service provider data centers are INCLUSIVE of colocation facilities. This is the most granular public per-facility-type PUE breakdown available from an authoritative US government source. engine_id is ollama only as a schema placeholder: facility metric, no engine.
notes: Closet: the worst space type in the table and still common, because roughly half of US servers sit in server rooms and closets. A PUE of 2.0 means half of all electricity at this site does no computing at all. Single-line failure of a closet is also why these are the facilities least able to absorb dense AI racks. CAVEAT ON AGE: these are 2014 values and the 2016 report frames the 2020 trajectory separately (dynamic range, consolidation). For a current planning number prefer the 2025 Update's 1.45 national all-equipment average. The 2014 table is retained because the modern public sources publish only fleet or national AVERAGES - this table is the only public breakdown that shows a colocation-class facility is closer to 1.9 than to 1.2.
